rejected_videos.reason: The video introduces supervised learning and input–target examples, partially supporting f1, but does not teach prediction-time input availability (f2) or a task record specifying prediction unit, target, prediction time and target horizon (f4). The brief spam-frequency discussion at 202–222 seconds does not explain the population and conditioning-group denominators required by f3. No standalone range adequately teaches the intended prediction-task framing; the relevant explanations also reference earlier examples or expand into model training and task-type taxonomy outside this tile's allowed knowledge.

The video teaches array dimensionality, shape and multidimensional indexing, not validation of a declared model-input contract. It does not inspect dtype, check a.ndim == 2 or declared feature/batch counts, conditionally raise ValueError for contract violations, or demonstrate assert checks for valid, boundary and failure cases. The ValueError at 172 seconds comes from constructing a ragged array, not explicit input validation. The shape explanation at 212–268 seconds relies on the previously constructed three-dimensional character array. No clean standalone range covers the required validation facts.

No clean standalone segment teaches model-boundary shape validation. The video demonstrates array creation, reshape, flatten, ravel, and view/copy behavior, rather than validating a declared batch/feature contract. It does not inspect ndim, shape, and dtype together (f1), check rank and feature count (f2), check batch length using shape[0] after rank validation (f3), conditionally raise ValueError for invalid input (f4), or demonstrate assertion checks for valid, boundary, and failure cases (f5). The reshaping demonstration cannot substitute for these acceptance checks; later chapters also depend on arrays created earlier and introduce untaught manipulation and memory-sharing concepts.

No clean standalone segment covers the required precision–memory selection procedure. The numerical demo at 49–257 seconds shows dtype inspection, integer range limits, numerical bit widths, and nbytes, but does not explain a.size × a.itemsize or the exclusion of non-element overhead, demonstrate floating-point precision loss, or compare cast values with reference values using arithmetic differences. The astype demo at 430–501 seconds demonstrates conversion and decimal truncation, but begins with an array established earlier and still lacks reference-value acceptance checks. Combining these sections would include unrelated Boolean, string, and object material without closing the coverage gaps.
